title: Customer lifecycle containment protocol - at-risk account triage & exec escalation
body:
Purpose:
This is a working containment protocol for high-risk subscription churn windows. The playbook defines: a compact risk-scoring rubric, immediate containment actions, tiered save plays (technical, commercial, executive), escalation SLAs, communication templates, and post-save learning steps.

Context and intent:
- Goal: buy time and restore confidence so commercial negotiations and technical remediation can close renewal gaps.
- This is intentionally lightweight — usable as a 30-60 minute response framework for CS, Solutions Eng, and GTM leaders.
- Use when: automated health signals + account behavior indicate elevated churn probability and deal is within 90 days of renewal.

Risk scoring (quick rubric):
- Health score components (weights): usage 35%, errors/incidents 20%, NPS/CSAT 15%, feature adoption 20%, billing/issues 10%.
- Score bands: 0-39 (P0 - Critical), 40-59 (P1 - High), 60-79 (P2 - Moderate), 80-100 (P3 - Low).
- Trigger: any P0 or P1 within 90 days of renewal => start containment protocol.

Containment timeline and SLAs:
- 0-2 hours: initial triage. Assign owner, confirm signals, and run checklist.
- 2-24 hours: containment actions (technical hotfixes, temporary credits, executive intro).
- 24-72 hours: stabilization actions and alignment meeting with customer execs.
- >72 hours: move to recovery cadence or prepare formal commercial remediation.

Triage checklist (first 2 hours):
- Owner assigned (CS AE or CSM) + backup.
- Pull renewal date and contract terms.
- Confirm P0/P1 signals (list of events: spikes in 5xx, drop in DAU/requests, feature regressions, billing disputes).
- Snapshot: recent support tickets, incident timeline, top 3 product complaints.
- Quick win gate: can we restore basic functionality in <24h? If yes, prioritize technical/SE play.

Tiered save plays (choose combination):
1) Technical containment (SE + SRE):
  - Immediate: roll back or patch, enable safe-mode config, apply rate-limits, create temporary bypasses.
  - Outcome target: eliminate showstopper and reduce error rate by 90% within 24 hours.
2) Commercial cushioning (CS + Finance):
  - Options: one-time service credit, renewal proration, short-term invoice hold, extended pilot.
  - Rules: commercial remedies must be pre-approved by finance for accounts < $50k ARR; >$50k escalate to RevOps for approval.
3) Executive engagement (CS lead + sales + customer exec):
  - Exec intro email template (see templates).
  - Offer leadership review meeting within 72 hours.
  - Possible outcomes: committed roadmap change, dedicated engineering resource, or commercial concession.

Escalation matrix and contact ladder:
- P0 (Critical): CSM -> CS Lead -> Head of Customer Success -> CTO/Head of Product -> CEO (if enterprise $ assigned ARR > $250k). SLA: 4 hours to notify next level, 24 hours to get executive meeting scheduled.
- P1 (High): CSM -> CS Lead -> VP Sales (if contractual risk) -> Head of Customer Success. SLA: 24 hours to escalation.

Communication templates (copy/paste):
- Initial exec intro (subject): "Request: quick leadership touchpoint — [Customer] renewal & critical issues"
  Body snippet: "Hi [ExecName], I'm Maya Thompson, head CSM. We're seeing a critical disruption impacting [product area]. Proposed next step: 30-minute leadership review within 72 hours to agree stabilization and renewal path. We've started technical containment. TL;DR: impact, immediate remediation, ask."

- Customer status update (24h): short bullets: what we fixed, what we are monitoring, next steps, owner contact.

Decision rules for commercial concessions:
- If technical containment fails within 72 hours and risk remains P0/P1, consider 1 of: one-time credit up to 2% ARR, renewal extension up to 60 days, or product roadmap commitment with clear acceptance criteria.
- All concessions require documented Rationale + ROI analysis and approval chain noted in linked_artifacts.

Operational playbook items (runbook):
- Ticketing tags: "renewal-risk" + account name; use labels for P0/P1.
- Dashboard: daily snapshot of active containments and outcomes. Owner updates in Slack channel #cs-escapes with 2x daily standups while active.
- Template for internal blameless post-mortem after resolution.

Metrics to track during a containment:
- Time to first response, time to containment success (error reduction), renewal sentiment shift (NPS change), commercial concession cost, net retention movement post 90 days.

Playbook governance and review cadence:
- Quarterly review of playbook effectiveness; reconcile concessions to actual retention impact.
- Post-mortem within 7 business days after containment ends; submit lessons to Confluence page linked above.

Quick operational notes / "notes to self":
- Keep templates short; execs hate long threads.
- Maintain a small pre-approved concession menu to avoid approval bottlenecks during urgent windows.
- Consider bundling technical milestones into the renewal contract as an addendum when roadmap commitments are promised.

Open questions (items to finalize):
- Set concrete thresholds for ARR bands that change approval requirements.
- Define authorized finance approvers for mid-market concessions.
- Finalize central dashboard owner (product analytics vs. CS Ops).

Appendices (snippets to copy into emails / Slack):
- Exec intro: "Hi [Name], we value our partnership and want to ensure continuity. We've identified a critical issue affecting X customers in your cluster. We've applied an immediate fix and propose a 30m leadership sync. Can you do [3 slots]?"
- Internal Slack ping: "ACTION: containment for [acct] (P0). Owner: @X. SE engaged. Need finance pre-approval for 2% credit if unresolved by 72h."

End notes:
This is a working draft — please test in a non-prod mock (run a practice containment during a dry-run week) and add realistic examples from recent saves. After two validated saves, convert to a formal CS SOP and push to Confluence for company-wide access.
